newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Clerides pledges to push for Cyprus solution.
newsitem.headline: Clerides pledges to push for Cyprus solution.

text.p: Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides said on Saturday he was willing to negotiate in a spirit of goodwill to reunite the eastern Mediterranean island.
But he added that he would not accept a solution that would compromise the existence of Greek Cypriots.

In a speech on the eve of the 23rd anniversary of the Turkish invasion of northern Cyprus, Clerides expressed hope that the latest United Nations initiative to resolve the conflict splitting the island would succeed.
"We shall not hesitate to say "yes" if we judge this to be in the interests of Cyprus's Hellenism.
"But we shall not hesitate to say 'No' if we are not being led to a solution which is just, viable and functionable," Clerides said.

Turkey invaded on July 20, 1974, in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece. Some 30,000 troops are stationed in northern Cyprus, declared a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in 1983 but recognised only by Ankara.
Turkish Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit, who ordered the invasion, is expected to attend celebrations in northern Cyprus on Sunday.
Clerides recently met Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash in northern New York state in an attempt to revive stalled negotiations on reunification as a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation.
The Greek Cypriot community is prepared to show the same goodwill at the second round of talks scheduled for Montreux, Switzerland, in mid-August, Clerides said.

"We are all hoping that this process which has already started will be the real commencement of an unprecedented effort to find a solution," he said, urging both sides on the island to envisage a common future.
"We gave an obligation to find a solution which will close the wounds of the past, pushing aside hatred, suspicion and the feelings of insecurity in the two communities," Clerides said.
"We have an obligation to create a new prospect of peace and security based on international law ... so we can enjoy the fruits of harmonic co-existence and cooperation in Europe."
Clerides and Denktash have agreed to meet in the Cyprus capital Nicosia before the second round to discuss humanitarian issues.
The Greek Cypriot side is expected to raise the issue of over 1,600 people unaccounted for since 1974, and the living conditions of about 500 Greek Cypriots in the Turkish-held areas.
